alex: quick sync: i ran a cost diffs sweep for our current ingest windowing settings — looks like a ~12% extra cost for traces with late-arrival reassembly vs when we align windows to event watermarks

maria: ugh, that’s higher than I expected. is this mostly due to overlapping windows causing duplicate storage/processing?

alex: yeah. two main factors: 1) overlapping tumbling windows + late arrivals means we re-process same spans into two windows, 2) dedupe TTL is too long so de-dup isn't trimming earlier records quickly enough

jon: can you share the test config and dataset? was this on prod-ish traffic shape or a toy trace set?

alex: ran on 24h sampled production traces (10% sample) and a synthetic bursty workload. config snippet I used:
```yaml
window_type: tumbling
window_ms: 60000
allowed_lateness_ms: 300000
dedupe_ttl_ms: 600000
emit_on_watermark: true
```

sam: three quick tradeoffs we need to consider: cost vs queryability vs tail-latency. shorter windows reduce cost but make cross-window queries harder and hurt latency for queries expecting full trace immediately

maria: can we do hybrid windows? e.g. align windows to service-specific watermarks for traces heavy on RPC fanout, and longer windows for rare long-tail traces

alex: that’s one option. another is adaptive allowed_lateness per tenant or per service: infer per-service 95th arrival time and set allowed_lateness to that percentile + buffer

jon: adaptive sounds nice but adds complexity to rollout. Where would we store those per-service heuristics? small metadata table in the config service?

sam: +1 metadata store. low read/write QPS. but we should also define safe fallbacks if heuristics break (e.g., global default of 5m).

maria: what about de-dupe TTL tuning? If we can reduce dedupe_ttl_ms we can reduce double-counting cost without changing windowing much

alex: true. tradeoff there is risk of missing truly late duplicates which can break attribution. but maybe we can do tiered TTL: short TTL by default, and extended TTL for traces tagged "long-tail" via header/envelope

jon: could we fingerprint traces and do streaming incremental stitch instead of full-window dedup? i.e., maintain a small LRU KV of recent span ids with last-seen timestamp, evict aggressively when memory pressure high
sam: that's effectively what dedupe TTL + LRU would be. question is mem/OOM bounds. per-tenant worst-case can be bad. we need eviction heuristics and circuit breaker to fall back to coarser windows

ingest-bot: deploy bot: staging rollout of ingest-windowing-v2 started by @alex at 2026-05-12T14:18:00Z :rocket:

maria: perf question: how do metrics and logs differ here? traces are multi-span and suffer from reassembly cost; metrics are already pre-aggregated so smaller impact. logs vary wildly by size and arrival pattern

alex: exactly. propose we separate config surface: windowing.policy.traces vs .metrics vs .logs and allow per-source defaults + per-service overrides

jon: okay, implementation plan sketch: 1) add per-service allowed_lateness heuristic producer to stats pipeline (runs in analytics), 2) metadata store + simple API, 3) change ingest to consult metadata and fallback to global default, 4) reduce dedupe_ttl default to 2m and enable long-tail tag to extend TTL

maria: ops: add pagination to our cost-reporting dashboard to show cost delta per-tenant when we enable heuristics. we need an easy rollback knob if cost spikes

sam: also add alerting: if dedupe rate drops > 30% after rollout or cost/spike > 20% vs baseline, auto-disable heuristics and page the oncall

alex: i'll draft an RFC for this with the implementation plan and a simple rollout checklist (staging -> canary 5% -> canary 25% -> 100)

jon: please include perf numbers from your test and an estimate of engineering effort. include a runbook for troubleshooting double-counting and missing-attribution cases

maria: sounds good. small UX ask: add a console view that surfaces per-service inferred lateness percentile and the current effective window so product teams can opt-in quickly

alex: noted. i'll put the RFC up by EOD tomorrow and @sam can review the SLO/alert pieces

sam: will do. thanks! :thumbsup:
